en: 2  Principles True in Every Country
zh: 第二章　每个国家都成立的原理

en: In 1863 Ismaʿil Pasha, the Ottoman ruler in Cairo, gave one hundred acres of land to his coffee maker. He gave another hundred to his head barber. He had succeeded his uncle Saʿid as viceroy in January of that year, and within eighteen months he allocated to those around him more than sixty thousand acres of the Nile valley. The recipients were military officers and high officials, family members and household staff. In the same short period he also added more than fifty thousand acres to his own estates.
zh: 1863年，奥斯曼帝国驻开罗的统治者伊斯梅尔帕夏（Ismaʿil Pasha）把一百费丹土地赐给了他的咖啡师，又赐给他的首席理发师一百费丹。当年1月，他继叔父赛义德（Saʿid）之位成为总督；在此后十八个月内，他把尼罗河谷六万多费丹土地分赐给身边的人。受赐者包括军官、高级官员、家族成员和家仆。同一短时期内，他还把自己的地产扩大了五万多费丹。

en: To Europeans, actions like these expressed everything that was wrong with the East. They exemplified the shortcoming for which colonial officials liked to criticize “native” systems of rule: their arbitrariness. Compared to the universal rules of a modern system of law, native government proceeded by personal decision and the caprice of power. “With respect to general propositions,” wrote an English administrator in India, “I have yet seen no reason to admit that principles, unquestionably true in every other country, should not be applicable in Bengal. It is in the nature of justice and good government to deduce its arrangements from undisputed points of original right. It is in the nature of arbitrary power to make exceptions.”

In non-European government the exceptional was the rule; power gained its strength from its arbitrariness. Modern government, like modern science, the European believed, was based upon principles true in every country. Its strength lay in its universalism.
zh: 在欧洲人看来，这类行动表明了东方的一切弊病。它们例证了殖民官员喜欢用来批评“土著”统治制度的缺陷：任意性。与近代法体系的普遍规则相比，土著政府凭个人决定和权力的无常运转。“就一般命题而言，”一位英国驻印度行政官员写道，“我至今没有理由承认，在别的任何国家都毫无疑问成立的原理，到了孟加拉就不适用。从不容置疑的原始权利出发推导制度安排，是正义和良好政府的本性。使自己的意志成为例外，则是专断权力的本性。”
在非欧洲的统治中，例外就是常规；权力从任意性中获得力量。欧洲人相信，现代政府犹如现代科学，建立在每个国家都成立的原理之上，其力量在于它的普遍主义。

en: This language belongs to an earlier century. But the views it expresses remain current. At the end of the twentieth century, the law of property reappeared at the center of Egypt’s political and economic life. As chapters 8 and 9 of this book describe, a program of political and economic restructuring reasserted the primacy of property rights as the institutional framework for the introduction of market relations. The universal rules of property were to replace the system of arbitrary political controls, special claims, and institutional exceptions that had restricted their operation. The political economy of Egypt was to be reestablished on the basis of principles true in every country.
zh: 这套语言属于更早的世纪，但它所表达的观点至今仍在流行。20世纪末，产权法重新出现在埃及政治和经济生活的中心。正如本书第8、9章所述，一场政治与经济重组计划重新确立了产权的首要地位，把它当作引入市场关系的制度框架。普遍的产权规则将取代限制其运作的任意政治控制、特殊要求和制度性例外。埃及的政治经济将基于在每个国家都成立的原理而重建。

en: the rule of property
zh: 产权的统治

en: How is the general character of law produced? How do the rules of property achieve the quality of being universal? There is no straightforward answer to this question. Modern jurisprudence sees law as self-establishing, existing as a system of rules whose validity is established only by other rules.

Modern economics sees the existence of property as self-evident, representing an axiomatic set of rules without which the act of exchange could not occur. In the positive accounts of law and economics, the genealogy of what is taken to be a universal system of rules is not open to investigation. This is inevitable, for if the axiomatic had its origins in particular histories and political acts, its claim to universalism would be lost.
zh: 法律的普遍品格是如何产生的？产权规则如何获得普遍性？这个问题没有直接答案。现代法学把法律视为自我确立的，是一个规则体系，其效力只由其他规则确立。
现代经济学把产权的存在视为自明的，认为它是一组公理式规则，没有它，交换行为便无从发生。在法学和经济学的实证论述中，被视为普遍规则体系之谱系，并不在考察范围之内。这是不可避免的：因为如果公理式的东西起源于特定的历史和政治行为，其普遍主义的主张就会丧失。

en: In Cairo, the answer to this question about the origin of modern property rights was first formulated in 1882. The British occupied the country that year, following a political crisis caused by Ismaʿil’s debts to European banks. They set up the Commission of Enquiry into the Land Tax, whose purpose was to examine property rights and taxes and propose measures for their reform.

These would remove irregularities from the tax system and increase the revenue, to pay off what was owed to Rothschilds and the other banks. The reforms required a cadastral survey to establish the owner and tax rate of each plot of land. This was not completed until after the turn of the century, so the revenue reforms had to wait. But right away the Ministry of Finance published a study of property relations, La Propriété foncière en Egypte. Written by the secretary to the Commission of Enquiry, the study explained property claims in the country in terms of the history of a concept: the evolution of the right of private ownership.
zh: 在开罗，关于现代产权起源的这个问题，首次在1882年得到回答。那一年，英国人在一场由伊斯梅尔对欧洲银行的债务所引发的政治危机之后占领了埃及。他们设立了土地税调查委员会，其目的是审查产权与税收，并提出改革措施。

这些措施将清除税收制度中的不规则之处、增加收入，以偿还欠罗斯柴尔德家族和其他银行的债务。改革需要地籍测量，以确定每一块土地的所有者和税率。这项工作直到20世纪之交以后才完成，因此税收改革不得不等待。但财政部随即出版了一项关于财产关系的研究——《埃及的土地产权》（La Propriété foncière en Egypte）。该研究由调查委员会秘书撰写，以概念史的方式解释该国的产权主张：私有制权利的演变。

en: The author drew on the work of contemporary French writers to argue that under the laws of the Ottoman Empire, which had ruled Cairo since 1517, all land was considered the property of the state.

French scholars had popularized this interpretation of Ottoman practice to justify the seizure of village land by French settlers in Algeria. Private property, they believed, was the foundation of civilization. Its absence in the territories of the Ottoman Empire demonstrated the uncivilized state of Muslim peoples and the progress that colonization would bring them.

This progress would come in the form of ideas. European legal principles, it was said, were based upon universal principles that can be applied uniformly to particular cases, by the process of abstracting from a particular circumstance to the general principle that governs it. Drawing on elements of this colonial view to portray a similar transition toward modernity in the Nile valley, the Ministry of Finance study became the text on which subsequent histories of the Egyptian law of property depended.
zh: 作者借助同时代法国作家的著作论证：自1517年以来统治开罗的奥斯曼帝国的法律之下，全部土地都被视为国家财产。
法国学者把这种对奥斯曼实践的阐释通俗化，以替法国定居者在阿尔及利亚夺取村庄土地辩护。他们相信，私有财产是文明的基础。奥斯曼帝国领土上私有财产的缺失，证明了穆斯林民族的未开化状态，也证明了殖民将给他们带来进步。
这种进步将以观念的形式到来。据称，欧洲法律原理以普遍原理为基础，可以通过从具体情况抽象出支配它的普遍原理，把普遍原理一致地适用于具体情况。财政部的研究借用了这种殖民观点的要素，来描绘尼罗河谷类似的现代性转变；它由此成为随后关于埃及财产法史的著作所依赖的文本。

en: Before the development of twentieth-century economics and jurisprudence, which offered ways to be silent about the genealogy of what claims to be universal, this kind of account was the only way, outside theology, to explain the general character of law. Law could claim to be universal, and thus nonarbitrary, only be appearing as the expression of civilization. The growth of civilization represented the spread of the principle of human reason, which overcame the limits of habit, prejudice, caprice, and ignorance. The faculty of reason gave men the power to step outside these local constraints, it was thought, and thus acquire a universal vision and understanding. European colonialism, understood as the contemporary expression of the spread of civilization and reason, established the abstract forms of law, in relation to which particular histories of the right of property could be written. Such histories occurred as the local expression or realization of this universal abstraction.
zh: 在20世纪法学和经济学发展出各种对“声称普遍之物”的谱系保持沉默的方式之前，这种叙述是神学之外解释法律普遍品格的唯一方式。法律只有表现为文明的表达，才能声称自己是普遍的，从而是非任意的。文明的成长代表了人类理性原则的传播，而理性原则克服了习惯、偏见、任意和愚昧的限制。据信，理性能力使人有能力走出这些地方性约束，从而获得普遍的视野和理解。欧洲殖民主义被理解为文明和理性传播的当代表现，它确立了法律的抽象形式；相对于这些形式，关于产权历史的个别叙述才得以书写。这类历史作为这一普遍抽象的地方性表达或实现而出现。

en: A certain contradiction is apparent. The virtues of a universal right of private property were articulated to support seizing land by force in North Africa. The land could be taken because those who farmed it had not heard of this universal right. The principle of property was presented as the opposite of arbitrary power or coercion, represented by the state ownership of land; but it justified a violent exercise of power, and in fact was established by this violence. The British were now articulating the same principle in Cairo, a city they had seized by force after first bombarding and destroying a large section of the country’s second city, Alexandria. Private property was seen as the reversal of the old order of state ownership. Law based on private rights represented a rupture with the previous world of arbitrary and despotic power. Yet many of the property claims that were to be consolidated as private rights, especially the largest ones, came into being through the “arbitrary” grants that Ismaʿil had made, and those of his uncles and grandfather before him. The author of the Ministry of Finance study, Yacoub Artin, was himself a product of this history of large estates. His grandfather, Sukias Tcherakian, an Armenian from Istanbul, moved to Cairo in 1812 soon after Ismaʿil’s grandfather, Mehmed Ali, came to power to manage the estates of one of Mehmed Ali’s sons.
Rather than there being a rupture, the old had helped form the new.
zh: 某种矛盾显而易见。普遍私有产权的优点被用来支持在北非以武力夺取土地。之所以能夺取土地，是因为耕种它的人从未听说过这项普遍权利。产权原则被说成是专断权力或强制的对立面——后者由国家土地所有制代表；但它为暴力行使权力辩护，事实上正是由这种暴力确立的。英国人如今在开罗宣扬同一原则；他们先炮击并摧毁了埃及第二大城市亚历山大港的大片城区，随后以武力占领了这座城市。私有财产被视为对旧的国有制秩序的颠倒。以私权为基础的法律，意味着与先前专断、专制权力世界的决裂。然而，后来被固化为私权的许多产权主张，尤其是最大的那些，正是通过伊斯梅尔及其叔父、祖父先前的“任意”赏赐产生的。财政部研究报告的作者雅各布·阿尔廷（Yacoub Artin）本身就是这种大地产史的产物。他的祖父苏基亚斯·切拉基安（Sukias Tcherakian）是来自伊斯坦布尔的亚美尼亚人，1812年迁到开罗；此前不久，伊斯梅尔的祖父穆罕默德·阿里（Mehmed Ali）掌权，阿尔廷的祖父为其一个儿子管理地产。
与其说存在决裂，不如说旧事物帮助形成了新事物。

en: The history of private property is rather silent on the conditions that produced it and the precedents incorporated into it. In fact it is silent on a lot more, as we will see. Presented as a history of legislation, of an abstraction, it has little to say about how private property was actually constituted in a particular place. The abstract arrives from elsewhere, and its particular histories are incidental rather than part of its nature. If its emergence had something to do with individual appropriations, exceptional decisions, or acts of violence, these belonged to the past, from which the present was now ruptured. The break in history caused by the colonial occupation, by the arrival of modernity and civilization, helped to establish the universal character of law. The ad hoc, violent, and exceptional character of the law of property was entirely hidden by the presentation of law as something abstract, as a universal rule, with its origins elsewhere, applied to particular circumstances.
zh: 私有制史对它赖以产生的条件以及被纳入其中的先例往往沉默。事实上，正如我们将看到的，它沉默的东西远不止这些。它被呈现为一部立法史、一部抽象概念史，却几乎不谈私有财产在特定地方实际上是如何构成的。抽象物来自别处，其特殊历史只是偶然插曲，而非其本质的一部分。如果私有财产的出现与个人占有、例外决定或暴力行为有关，这些都属于过去；现在已与那个过去断裂。殖民占领、现代性和文明的到来所造成的断裂，帮助确立了法律的普遍品格。产权法的事例性、暴力性和例外性，完全被一种法律呈现方式掩盖了：法律被表现为某种抽象之物、一条普遍规则，起源于别处，再被适用于具体情况。

en: Compared to Artin’s study of 1882, we have a better understanding today of landholding in the Ottoman Empire before the colonial occupations. We know that the view that all property was “owned” by the state is too simple and that for several centuries land in the Nile Delta had been treated as something that individuals could buy and sell.

We also know that landholding did not refer to land as an object, to which single individuals claimed an absolute right. It referred to a system of multiple claims, and not to the land itself but its revenue. The claimants included the Ottoman ruler, the ruler’s local representative, the legal-religious authorities, the cultivators themselves, and other customary claimants within the countryside, such as the indigent. The doctrine of state ownership of land did not correspond to the modern notion of property but registered the ruler’s political claim to a share of the revenue, while also acknowledging both the revenue claims of local political forces and the subsistence claims of the cultivator and other members of the village.

The network of claims, moreover, involved not just the land but a variety of processes and relations: grain as distinct from other crops, trees and their fruits, grazing rights, the supply of water, the maintenance of irrigation works, and so on. The claims were related to a wider discourse of justice and reciprocity reproduced in social practice. They were not fixed in an abstract code of law, but were guided by legal precedent and by prescriptions developed in response to actual circumstances and events.
zh: 与阿尔廷1882年的研究相比，我们对殖民占领前奥斯曼帝国的土地占有有了更好的理解。我们知道，所有财产都由国家“所有”的观点过于简单；我们也知道，几个世纪以来，尼罗河三角洲的土地一直被视为个人可以买卖之物。
我们还知道，土地占有并不指作为对象的土地，也不指某个个人对土地主张绝对权利。它指的是一套多重主张体系，指向的不是土地本身，而是土地的收益。主张者包括奥斯曼统治者、统治者在地方的代表、合法—宗教权威、耕种者本人，以及乡村中其他习惯性主张者，例如贫民。国家拥有土地这一学说，并不等同于现代的财产观念，而是记录了统治者对一份收益的政治主张，同时也承认地方政治势力的收益主张以及耕种者和其他村民的维生主张。
而且，这张主张网络不仅涉及土地，还涉及各种过程和关系：谷物与其他作物的区别、树木及其果实、放牧权、供水、灌溉设施的维护，等等。这些主张与一套关于正义和互惠的更广泛话语相关，并在社会实践中得到再生产。它们并未固定在一部抽象法典中，而是由法律先例以及针对实际情形和事件制定的规定来引导。

en: This understanding opens up further questions. How was it possible to reduce the productive processes of the countryside to the single issue of who controlled the land? How was the question of its control moved away from the competing claims and obligations of those who lived on the land and those who ruled them, and turned into a “right” that could be exercised absolutely, even by a person who had no relation to the place? How were these issues abstracted from forms of justice and reciprocity recognized (sometimes only in their violation) at the level of agricultural life, and located elsewhere—in the city, in its courts and police forces, and at some still more distant and abstract level, in propositions “true in every country”? How, in short, did modern law acquire its power and authority?
zh: 这一理解引出进一步的问题。乡村的生产过程如何可能被归结为“谁控制土地”这单一问题？土地控制问题如何从居住土地者和统治土地者的相互竞争的主张与义务中移开，变成一项可以绝对行使的“权利”，甚至可由与当地毫无关系的人行使？这些问题如何从农业生活中得到承认的（有时只在其被违反时得到承认的）正义与互惠形式中抽象出来，被置于别处——置于城市、法院和警察力量之中，甚至置于某个更遥远、更抽象的层面，即“在每个国家都成立”的命题之中？简言之，现代法律是如何获得其权力与权威的？

en: Let us return for a moment to Ismaʿil’s method of establishing claims to the land. In September 1863, to take a representative example, he issued the following instructions to his secretary of the treasury:
zh: 让我们暂时回到伊斯梅尔建立土地主张的方法。以1863年9月的一个代表性例子来说，他向财政书记发出了如下指示：

en: We have decided that three hundred acres are to be granted as an estate to His Lordship Nuri Bey, Governor of Sharqiyya. We have given an order to His Excellency the Inspector of the Lower Nile to have the said lands surveyed, their boundaries marked, and the list of the boundaries sent to the treasury. As soon as the list of boundaries reaches you, you are to record them and issue from the tax registry the required title deed in the name of the aforementioned and send it to him. This is the reason we have written this to you.
zh: 我们已决定，将三百费丹土地作为一处产业授予谢尔基亚省省长努里贝伊（Nuri Bey）阁下。我们已命令下尼罗河巡视官对上述土地进行测量，标定地界，并将地界清单送交国库。地界清单一到你处，你应立即登记，并从税收登记处签发以上述人士名义所需的产权证书，送交给他。此即我们致函于你的缘由。

en: Power seems to operate through a chain of personal orders and interconnected prerogatives rather than a generalized regime of government. It is not exactly arbitrary. The document refers to a legal process of recording, boundary marking, and bookkeeping. But the written record that results does not invoke any universal rule. In fact, it insists on its own specificity: “This is the reason we have written this to you.” Compared to the universal rules of a modern system of law, the document, and the actions and claims it performs, appears not so much ad hoc, but as a form of power whose specificity is not disguised. The law announces its specificity, tracing its own steps. The act of granting land, the inspector’s survey of the boundaries, the placing of boundary stones, the recording of measurements and sending them to Cairo, listing them in the taxation register, and issuing the title deed: all these acts are prescribed in the decree. The performance of the law will gain its authority from following this particular sequence of acts.
zh: 权力似乎通过一连串个人命令和相互关联的特权来运作，而不是通过一套普遍化的治理体制。它并不完全是任意的。文件提到登记、标界和记账的法律程序。但由此产生的书面记录并未援引任何普遍规则，反而坚持自身的特殊性：“此即我们致函于你的缘由。”与现代法体系的普遍规则相比，这份文件及其所实施的行动和主张，与其说是临时性的，不如说是一种不掩饰其特殊性的权力形式。法律宣告自己的特殊性，并追踪自己的步骤。授予土地的行为、巡视官丈量地界、安放界石、记录测量并送往开罗、将其列入税收登记簿、签发产权证书：所有这些行为都由这份敕令规定。法律的施行将从遵循这一特定行为序列中获得权威。

en: The order of private property that replaced this was just as particularistic. It, too, was based on individual acts, orders, seizures, descriptions, and inscriptions. But these processes were reorganized so that some seemed particular and others general: some appeared fixed, singular, anchored to a specific place and moment, like objects, while others appeared mobile, general, present everywhere at once, universal, unquestionably true in every place, and therefore abstract. One set of actions, people, and sites was fixed in position as “land” and “peasants,” made into objects to supervise and control. At the same time a series of removals, rearrangements, delaying maneuvers, simplifications, and silences established other sites and other actions as what seems the opposite of this: nonlocal, outside actuality, and therefore universal. This was to create the effect of a fundamental difference: land versus law, the particular versus the general, the physical versus the abstract, thing versus idea, force versus order. To understand how this difference was made we have to reopen the connections between what was separated, follow the links from one action to another, and see how one set of elements in this relationship was subordinated, removed, reserved, or silenced. This will bring to light what is buried when we write theories of “property,” “law,” and “the state,” when we begin with metaphysical abstractions rather than asking what methods of politics and expertise divide the world into metaphysics on the one hand and mere physics on the other.
zh: 取代它的私有产权秩序同样特殊主义。它同样建立在个人行为、命令、夺取、描述和铭写之上。但这些过程被重新组织，以致一些显得特殊，另一些显得普遍：一些看似固定、单一、锚定于特定地点和时刻，像物体一样；另一些则显得可移动、普遍、无所不在，在任何地方都成立，因而抽象。一组行动、人物和场所被固定在“土地”和“农民”的位置上，成为接受监督和控制的对象。与此同时，一系列移除、重新安排、拖延、简化和沉默，把另一些场所和行动确立为看似与之相反的东西：非地方的、外在于现实的，从而是普遍的。这是为了制造一种根本差异的效果：土地对法律、特殊对普遍、物理对抽象、物对观念、力量对秩序。要理解这种差异是如何造成的，我们必须重新打开那些被分开之物之间的连接，沿一条行动线索追踪到另一条，看看这种关系中的一组要素如何被从属化、移除、保留或消音。这样就会照亮我们在书写“财产”“法律”和“国家”理论时所掩埋的东西——当我们从形而上学抽象出发，而不是追问哪些政治和专门知识的方法把世界划分为一边的形而上学和另一边的单纯物理学时。

en: putting villagers in their place
zh: 让村民各安其位

en: Cotton and sugarcane, the modern world’s two main industrial crops, did not grow in the temperate climates of Europe. They needed the warmth of semitropical zones, where northern Europeans found it difficult to work or settle. Over several hundred years the English and French had developed what many considered a sophisticated institution to solve this difficulty— the slave plantation. Developed in the Caribbean, it had been expanded by the Americans across the southern United States. The government in early nineteenth-century Cairo was keen to import modern European and American ways of doing things. In fact it sent its European-officered army to invade the Sudan in July 1820 to establish control over the sultanates that ruled the Upper Nile and import slaves to the north. However, the efforts at mass enslavement failed. A system of industrial agriculture based on the importation and private ownership of humans could not be introduced into the Nile valley. Instead, the government tried a number of different methods to create an industrial discipline among the existing agrarian communities. The result was a further series of failures.
zh: 棉花和甘蔗是现代世界的两大工业作物，却不生长在欧洲的温带气候中。它们需要亚热带地区的温暖，而北欧人发现那里难以劳作或定居。几百年来，英国人和法国人发展出一套被许多人视为精巧的制度来解决这一困难——奴隶种植园。它发展于加勒比地区，又被美国人扩展到美国南部。19世纪初的开罗政府热衷引进现代欧洲和美国的做事方式。事实上，它在1820年7月派出由欧洲军官指挥的军队入侵苏丹，以控制统治上尼罗河的各苏丹国，并向北输入奴隶。然而，大规模奴役的尝试失败了。以输入和私人拥有奴隶为基础的工业农业制度无法引入尼罗河谷。政府转而尝试多种方法，在既有农业社群中建立工业纪律。结果是一连串新的失败。

en: Before the nineteenth century methods of government in the parts of the Nile valley controlled from Cairo were based on dividing the revenue of the land. Farmers paid a part of their main crop—a food grain—to the authorities in exchange, they were told, for the security and justice that authority guaranteed. This method would not work with the modern industrial and export crops in demand in Europe, such as cotton and sugar, or opium. Farmers had no interest in growing a crop they could not eat, or process to serve local needs. The authorities, on the other hand, needed a way to take the whole crop. For the first time they needed a method of making farmers grow something they did not want and hand it over entirely. Or perhaps they had often thought of doing this but only now believed, thanks to the power of the new, disciplined army, that they had the means to achieve it. As John Bowring, friend of Jeremy Bentham and advisor to Mehmed Ali, later reported to the British parliament, “nothing but despotic authority would have forced the cultivation of many of those important articles such as cotton, opium, sugar, indigo, etc., of which Egypt furnishes so large a supply.”
Thus a “monopoly” system was introduced, backed by military discipline, that compelled villagers to grow certain crops and deliver them to government warehouses.
zh: 在19世纪以前，开罗所控制的尼罗河谷地区的统治方法以分割土地收益为基础。农民把主要作物——一种粮食谷物——的一部分交给当局，作为交换，他们被告知，权威将提供安全和正义。这种方法无法适用于欧洲所需的现代工业和出口作物，如棉花、甘蔗或鸦片。农民对种植一种自己不能吃、也无法加工以满足本地需要的作物毫无兴趣。另一方面，当局需要一种取走全部作物的办法。他们第一次需要一种方法，迫使农民种植自己不想种的东西，并把它全部交出。或许他们过去也常想这么做，但直到现在，凭借新的、有纪律的军队的力量，才相信自己拥有实现这一目标的手段。正如杰里米·边沁的朋友、穆罕默德·阿里的顾问约翰·鲍林（John Bowring）后来向英国议会报告的那样：“只有专断权威才能迫使人们种植棉花、鸦片、甘蔗、靛蓝等许多重要作物；埃及供应着大量此类作物。”
于是，一套由军事纪律支持的“垄断”制度被引入，迫使村民种植某些作物并交到政府仓库。

en: The response of the rural population was a straightforward one. Large numbers refused to farm and in many cases abandoned their villages. Tens of thousands deserted their homes and moved to agricultural regions outside government control, or escaped to Cairo and other towns, or moved further abroad to Palestine and Syria. The Ottoman governor, Mehmed Ali, responded by instituting a more elaborate system of overseers and penalties and ordering the confinement of peasants to their villages, with permits required for those who wished to travel outside their locality.
These measures failed to stop the exodus. In 1842 the authorities began to compile a register with the names of all those reported to have deserted their villages.

At the same time they introduced a new system, allocating officials of the ruling household, or in some cases local notables or merchants, the responsibility for the tax arrears of particular villages.
Yet desertion remained a serious problem, continuing under Mehmed Ali’s successors.
zh: 农村人口的反应很直接。大批人不愿耕作，许多人抛弃了村庄。数万人离开家园，迁往政府控制之外的农业地区，或逃到开罗和其他城镇，或远走巴勒斯坦和叙利亚。奥斯曼总督穆罕默德·阿里作出回应，设立更严密的监工和处罚制度，下令把农民限制在村庄内，凡想离开本地者须持许可证。
这些措施未能制止逃亡。1842年，当局开始编制登记册，记录所有据报逃离村庄者的姓名。
同时，他们引入新制度，让统治家族官员、有时是地方显贵或商人，为特定村庄的欠税负责。
然而，逃亡仍是严重问题，在穆罕默德·阿里的继任者治下依然如此。

en: The next response to the problem of keeping the rural population in place was a series of measures between 1847 and 1862 to restrict or eliminate the customary claims of those who abandoned their land. These are the regulations later assembled by the Ministry of Finance into the account of the emergence of private landownership discussed above. Cuno shows the regulations were concerned less with individual rights and more with stabilizing the existing land regime after the disruptive agrarian programs of the first half of the century.

While Cuno’s arguments are persuasive, we can state more specifically that the new laws were a response to the continuing crisis of desertion, legalizing the expropriation of the land of those who fled and seeking to deter others from fleeing. Four of the six provisions of the first land law in 1847 were concerned with limiting the claims of those who had deserted their land. Deserters who returned to claim land that had been allocated as a tax responsibility to someone else were entitled to recover only half the land and required to reimburse the taxes paid. The 1855 land law was an amendment to this regulation, setting further limits on the ability to recover land. After fifteen years returnees lost all rights to their land and would receive instead only a subsistence plot of between half an acre and three acres. An 1858 law reduced the period after which deserters lost all rights to their land to five years.

Despite these measures the problem of desertion continued. A further decree of December 7, 1862, not mentioned in the histories of landownership but confirming the preoccupation with desertion, was still more severe: any native who deserted his village would have his land seized and sold off after two months, unless he deserted during the cultivation season, in which case it would be seized and sold immediately.

Far from representing a gradual accumulation of rights by the individual, the land laws of the mid-nineteenth century represented a series of attempts to compel individuals to remain at work on the land and to confirm the seizure of land from those who fled.
zh: 对留住农村人口问题的下一轮回应，是1847至1862年间一系列限制或取消失地者习惯性主张的措施。这些规定后来被财政部汇编进上文讨论的私有土地所有权产生的叙述中。库诺（Cuno）表明，这些规定与其说关心个人权利，不如说是在19世纪上半叶破坏性的农业计划之后稳定既有土地制度。

库诺的论证有说服力，但我们可以更具体地说：新法律是对持续逃亡危机的回应，使没收逃亡者土地合法化，并试图阻止其他人逃亡。1847年第一部土地法的六项规定中，有四项旨在限制弃地者的主张。返回要求他人承担纳税责任的土地的逃亡者，只能收回一半土地，并须偿还已缴税款。1855年土地法是对这一规定的修正，进一步限制收回土地的能力。满十五年后，返回者丧失对土地的一切权利，只能获得半费丹至三费丹的维生份地。1858年的一项法律把逃亡者丧失全部土地权利的期限缩短为五年。
尽管采取了这些措施，逃亡问题仍在继续。1862年12月7日的一项敕令更严厉，却未被土地所有权史提及，它进一步印证了当局对逃亡问题的执意关注：任何逃离村庄的本地人，其土地将在两个月后被没收并出售；若他是在耕作季节逃离，则立即没收并出售。
19世纪中期的土地法远非个人权利逐步积累的体现，而是一系列迫使个人留在土地上劳作、并确认夺取逃亡者土地的尝试。

en: These measures were related to another process, also usually omitted from histories of private property: the incorporation or erasure of political communities that occupied the margin, neither outside nor completely within the jurisdiction of Cairo. Before the middle of the nineteenth century, most people inhabiting parts of the Nile valley beyond the immediate reach of Cairo lived in autonomous political communities referred to as tribes or emirates, and were relatively independent of the Cairene authorities.

Historical sources refer to these populations as ʿarab, a term usually translated as “Bedouin” and used in contrast to the fellahs, the settled villagers. Although the word ʿarab historically refers to the pastoral nomads of the desert, in the Nile valley large numbers of them farmed the land and lived in villages. What distinguished them from other villagers was not necessarily nomadism but their relative autonomy from Cairo and often their domination over the fellahs themselves. They lived on the geographical margin, partly within and partly beyond government control. Their lands were seldom registered or taxed, but they often payed some collective form of tribute. They were involved in agriculture but did not belong to the “peasantry.” They formed a complex economic and political borderland.
zh: 这些措施还与另一个过程有关，而这一过程通常也被排除在私有制史之外：那些占据边缘地带、既不在开罗管辖之外也不完全在其管辖之内的政治共同体的并入或抹除。19世纪中叶以前，居住在开罗直接控制范围之外的尼罗河谷地区的大多数人，生活在被称为部落或酋长国的自治政治共同体中，相对独立于开罗当局。

历史资料把这些人口称为ʿarab，这个词通常译为“贝都因人”，并与定居村民费拉赫（fellah）相对使用。尽管ʿarab一词在历史上指沙漠中的游牧民族，但在尼罗河谷，大量ʿarab耕种土地，居住在村庄里。把他们与其他村民区分开来的，不一定在于游牧，而在于他们相对独立于开罗，并且常常支配费拉赫本身。他们生活在地理边缘，部分在政府控制之内，部分在其外。他们的土地很少被登记或征税，但他们往往缴纳某种形式的集体贡赋。他们参与农业，却不属于“农民阶层”。他们构成一个复杂的经济和政治边缘地带。

en: The new control over the countryside involved eliminating these border forms of political life. Modern accounts of this process, assuming that the ʿarab were nomads, describe it as “the settlement of the Bedouin.”

In fact it involved, once again, the attempt to construct a new kind of control over their lands and livelihoods, and much of their so-called nomadism was simply the dislocation caused by this attempt. The government of Mehmed Ali initially recognized the Arab claims to land used for pasture or seasonal cultivation.
But from the 1840s, members of the ruling household began to take such land to create large estates for themselves.

Violent struggles broke out, and by the end of the 1850s the “Arab troubles,” as official sources refer to the conflict, had become so severe that large numbers had abandoned agriculture and moved with their herds to areas beyond the reach of government troops, or fled abroad.
zh: 对乡村的新控制包括消灭这些边缘地带的政治生活形式。现代论述假定ʿarab是游牧民，把这一过程描述为“贝都因人的定居化”。
事实上，它再次是试图对他们的土地和生计建立一种新的控制，而他们所谓的游牧，很大程度上不过是这种尝试造成的流离失所。穆罕默德·阿里政府起初承认阿拉伯人对用于放牧或季节性耕作的土地的主张。
但从19世纪40年代起，统治家族的成员开始夺取这类土地，为自己建立大型地产。
暴力冲突爆发了；到19世纪50年代末，官方材料所称的“阿拉伯人骚乱”已经严重到使大批人放弃农业，带着畜群迁往政府军队无法到达的地区，或逃往国外。

en: When Ismaʿil came to power in January 1863 and began granting estates to his officials and relatives, he was responding to a series of failures and increasingly violent reactions in the search for new methods of controlling the way crops were grown. He had spent the preceding years organizing new estates of his own in the south, developing the production of cotton and sugarcane and running a sugar refinery that was described as the country’s most impressive industrial project.
He brought the expertise acquired in the managing of sugar mills and plantations back to Cairo, and began reorganizing the whole country as a system of agricultural estates.
zh: 1863年1月伊斯梅尔掌权，开始把地产赐给官员和亲属；他这样做，是在回应寻找控制作物种植方式的新方法过程中一连串的失败和日益激烈的反抗。在此前几年，他一直在南方经营自己的新地产，发展棉花和甘蔗生产，并经营一家被描述为该国最令人瞩目的工业项目的糖厂。
他把管理糖厂和种植园所获得的专门知识带回开罗，开始把整个国家重组为一个农业地产体系。

en: In his first week in office he abrogated the 1862 law penalizing rural desertion. He ordered the governors of every province to draw up lists of those who had lost their land, together with the value of the land and the names of those who had taken it over. From now on natives who abandoned their land were to be treated according to established principles, which presumably meant restoring the five-year limit of the 1858 law.
He also encouraged the Arabs to return to their lands. To those without property he offered parcels of abandoned land, giving two acres to every household of five persons.

In exchange, the Arabs were required to submit to the authority of a military officer appointed in each district to oversee their affairs. They were to give the officer a list of the heads of the sections of each tribe, with the number of persons and a description of each individual enumerated “tribe by tribe, section by section, name by name.” The officer would then issue a permit with the name, physical description, and tribe of every individual under his authority. A person who wished to move from one tribal section to another, or one part of the country to another, required this permit to travel.
zh: 上任第一周，他就废除了1862年惩罚农村弃地行为的法律。他命令各省省长编制失去土地者的名单，附上土地价值和接管者的姓名。此后，放弃土地的本地人将按既定原则处理，这大概意味着恢复1858年法律规定的五年期限。
他还鼓励阿拉伯人回到自己的土地。他向没有财产的人提供小块弃地，每户五口人给两费丹。
作为交换，阿拉伯人必须接受各区任命的一名军官的管辖，由该军官监督他们的事务。他们须向这位军官提交各部落各分支首领的名单，并逐一列明人数和对每个人的描述，“一个部落一个部落、一个分支一个分支、一个名字一个名字”。军官随后为其管辖下的每个人签发许可证，写明姓名、体貌特征和所属部落。凡希望从一个部落分支迁往另一个分支，或从国内一个地方迁往另一个地方者，须持此许可证通行。

en: a mad fanatic and a communist
zh: 一个疯狂的狂热分子和一个共产主义者

en: We know very little about the impact of these events on people’s lives. Most of what we can learn about those lives is from the traces they left elsewhere. We know about the flight of villagers from the land largely through such sources as the further acts of dispossession with which government tried to punish them. On occasion, however, the violence of property making, which was also the violence of nation making, provoked a more concerted reaction. These events left larger traces, although still only partial.
zh: 我们对这些事件给人们生活造成的影响所知甚少。我们对这些人的生活所能了解的大部分，来自他们在别处留下的痕迹。我们之所以知道村民逃离土地，很大程度上是通过政府为惩罚他们而采取的进一步剥夺行动之类的材料。然而，产权的制造同时也是民族的制造，这种暴力有时会激起更协调一致的反抗。这些事件留下了更大的痕迹，尽管仍然只是局部的。

en: The uprising against British rule in India in 1857–58 provided a warning of what could develop, and the British were soon to bring the lessons they learned in India to Egypt. But the popular message from India arrived sooner, reaching the Upper Nile provinces of Jirja and Asyut, where Ismaʿil was building his sugar plantations. To convert flood basin agriculture to the year-round cultivation of cane, workers were digging the Ibrahimiyya Canal, the largest construction project ever undertaken in the Nile valley and reported to be the largest canal in the world, extending more than four hundred kilometers from Asyut to Cairo.
Both the cane plantations and the canal required large amounts of forced labor.
zh: 1857—1858年印度反抗英国统治的起义，预示了可能发生的事态；英国人很快就把他们在印度吸取的教训带到了埃及。但来自印度的民众信息来得更早，传到了上尼罗河的吉尔贾省和艾斯尤特省，伊斯梅尔正在那里兴建甘蔗种植园。为了把洪泛盆地农业改造为甘蔗的全年种植，工人们在挖掘易卜拉欣尼亚运河；这是尼罗河谷有史以来最大的建设工程，据报道也是世界上最大的运河，从艾斯尤特延伸至开罗，全长四百多公里。
甘蔗种植园和运河都需要大量强制劳动力。

en: A sign of the impending troubles was a murder that took place in June 1863 in Tanagha, a village about thirty kilometers south of the town of Asyut, in an area where Ismaʿil had acquired several sugar estates. The victim was someone of significance, at least to Ismaʿil, for the viceroy personally ordered that all firearms be confiscated from the inhabitants of the village and that the same be done in any village in Asyut province where a killing occurred. If any villager was subsequently found with a weapon, the village head was to be dismissed and his sons and relatives forbidden to assume the headship.
zh: 即将到来的动荡的一个征兆，是1863年6月在塔纳加发生的一起谋杀。塔纳加是艾斯尤特镇以南约三十公里的一个村庄，伊斯梅尔在这一带购置了几处甘蔗地产。受害者是个重要人物，至少对伊斯梅尔而言如此，因为总督亲自下令没收该村居民的一切火器，而且艾斯尤特省任何村庄若发生杀人事件，也照此办理。如果此后发现任何村民持有武器，村长将被撤职，其子侄亲属不得接任村长。

en: In the winter of 1864–65 the crisis came. In October Ismaʿil took over a large estate, which included a sugar mill and steam pumps, at the village of Najʿ Hamadi, claiming the land had belonged to his elder brother Ahmad (who had been drowned in a railway accident six years earlier).
The difficulties created by the spread of plantations were aggravated by serious flooding in the autumn, which devastated the nearby town of Jirja and destroyed homes and crops throughout the region.

By February there were severe food shortages and most of the cattle were dead. Yet the government continued to impose burdens. Orders reached local officials to make a levy of camels to support the continued occupation of the Sudan; to begin work immediately on improved flood defenses at Jirja, requiring 1,085,000 hundredweight of stone; and to provide another fifty thousand men as forced laborers on the Ibrahimiyya Canal.

“The system of wholesale extortion and spoilation has reached a point beyond which it would be difficult to go,” wrote a European resident. “Egypt is one vast ‘plantation’ where the master works his slaves without even feeding them.”
zh: 1864—1865年冬天，危机爆发。10月，伊斯梅尔接管了纳杰·哈马迪村的一处大地产，其中包括一家糖厂和几台蒸汽抽水机，他声称这块土地属于他的兄长艾哈迈德（六年前在一起铁路事故中溺水身亡）。
种植园扩张造成的困难，又因秋季的严重洪水而加剧；洪水摧毁了附近的吉尔贾镇，毁掉了整个地区的房屋和庄稼。
到2月，粮食严重短缺，大部分牛只已经死亡。但政府仍继续加派负担。给地方官员的命令要求：征调骆驼以支持对苏丹的持续占领；立即动工改进吉尔贾的防洪设施，需要108.5万英担石料；再提供五万名强制劳工去修易卜拉欣尼亚运河。
“这种大规模勒索和掠夺的制度已经达到难以再进一步的地步，”一位欧洲侨民写道，“埃及就是一个巨大的‘种植园’，主人驱使他的奴隶干活，甚至不给他们饭吃。”

en: A month later an armed uprising broke out, beginning in the village of Qaw, near Jirja, and four neighboring villages, but reaching as far as Asyut forty kilometers to the north.

The revolt was led by Ahmad al-Shaqi, known as al-Tayyib, the Good, native of the village of Salamiyya, near Luxor, and said to be the disciple of an anticolonial religious militant from India who had escaped abroad after the defeat of the 1857–58 revolt and spent several years near Asyut. The seriousness of the uprising is indicated by the seniority of those sent to suppress it. Mehmed Fadil Pasha, inspector of the Upper Nile region, came by steamer from Cairo with an armed force, and Ismaʿil himself followed. The secretary of war, Ismaʿil Pasha Abu Jabal, commanded the troops. They burned Qaw and its four neighboring villages to the ground and sent the surviving male inhabitants as prisoners to the Sudan. The women and children were distributed among other villages. Ahmad al-Tayyib was rumored to have escaped, but his relatives from Salamiyya, men, women, and children, were taken in chains to Qina. Reports of the number of villagers who were killed ranged from several dozen to sixteen hundred. One eyewitness described how Fadil Pasha “had the men laid down by ten at a time and chopped with pioneer axes.” Fadil was rewarded after his return to Cairo with promotion to the Council of Justice.
zh: 一个月后，武装起义爆发，始于吉尔贾附近的考村和四个邻村，但蔓延到北面四十公里外的艾斯尤特。

起义由艾哈迈德·沙基（Ahmad al-Shaqi）领导，他被称为“泰伊卜”（al-Tayyib），意为“善者”，是卢克索附近萨拉米亚村人；据说他是一名来自印度的反殖民宗教斗士的门徒，此人在1857—1858年起义失败后逃往国外，并在艾斯尤特附近住了几年。派去镇压者的级别之高，说明了起义的严重程度。上尼罗河地区巡视官迈赫迈德·法迪勒帕夏率武装部队乘汽船从开罗赶来，伊斯梅尔本人随后也到了。陆军大臣伊斯梅尔帕夏·阿布·贾巴尔指挥部队。他们把考村及其四个邻村夷为平地，把幸存的男性居民作为囚犯送往苏丹。妇女和儿童被分散到其他村庄。有传言说艾哈迈德·泰伊卜逃脱了，但他来自萨拉米亚的亲属，无论男女老幼，都被戴上镣铐押往基纳。关于被杀村民人数的报道从几十人到一千六百人不等。一位目击者描述法迪勒帕夏如何“让人一次趴下十个，用工兵斧砍”。法迪勒回到开罗后获得奖赏，被提升进司法委员会。

en: British consular reports attributed the revolt to the labor that villagers were forced to supply on Ismaʿil’s estates. The food shortage had caused prices to jump, and local wages had also risen. Measures introduced in January to control prices from Cairo by setting up a Prices Committee and provincial Commerce Committees had failed to halt the increases.
The fixed wage of two and a half piastres a day that Ismaʿil had introduced on his estates two years earlier represented only one-quarter of prevailing wages by 1865.

Local reports agreed that although religious appeals provided al-Tayyib’s legitimation, his object was the new land regime. “He is a mad fanatic and a communist,” a European resident in the area was told. “He wants to divide all property equally and to kill all the Ulema.”

Ismaʿil blamed the events on the negligence of the governor of Jirja, whom he removed and put to trial. He also appointed a separate administrator for his estates in the south, divorcing their management from those in the Delta.
The effort to turn much of the region into his plantation was proving difficult.
zh: 英国领事报告把起义归因于村民被迫为伊斯梅尔的地产提供的劳动。粮食短缺导致物价飞涨，当地工资也上涨了。1月从开罗推出的措施——设立物价委员会和省商业委员会以控制物价——未能阻止价格继续上涨。
伊斯梅尔两年前在其地产上实行的每天两个半皮阿斯特的固定工资，到1865年只有通行工资的四分之一。
当地报告一致认为，尽管宗教号召为泰伊卜提供了合法性，但他的目标针对的是新的土地制度。“他是个疯狂的狂热分子，一个共产主义者，”当地一位欧洲侨民被告知，“他想把一切财产平均分配，还要杀光所有乌里玛。”
伊斯梅尔把事件归咎于吉尔贾省长的失职，将其撤职并送审。他还为南方地产另行任命了一名管理人，使其管理脱离三角洲的地产管理。
把该地区大部分地方变成他的种植园的企图，正变得越来越困难。

en: Despite the violence with which the government demonstrated its resolve, the problems of villagers abandoning the farming of overtaxed land and rejecting the authority of Cairo continued. In 1865 the viceroy issued a decree forbidding officials to grant anyone permission to abandon their land.

Later that year he ordered the sale of rights to all abandoned land, and of any cultivated land that was not registered in the tax registers, while the period after which those who deserted their villages lost their rights was reduced again, from five years to three.

Another order of the same year noted that despite the efforts at conciliation the Bedouin were still refusing to submit to the viceroy’s authority. Instructions were given that any Arab found in a town, at a market, on a road, or in any other place carrying a firearm was to be arrested.
Several orders were also issued in the same period to inspect and reorganize the country’s numerous prisons.

In June 1865, the inspector of the Lower Nile region reported a large increase in theft, including attacks at night on villages and isolated estates, in which property and animals were looted. Ismaʿil declared this to be the work of evil and malicious individuals, many of them former convicts, who had to be eliminated—by further incarceration. He ordered the head of every village and Arab tribe to round up within thirty days all “depraved and malicious persons and suspicious characters” in their localities. Those arrested were to be sent to the army or navy if fit, otherwise to labor in the stone quarries at the Nile Cataracts. If any such persons were found in their districts after thirty days, the headmen themselves would be punished.
zh: 尽管政府以暴力显示了决心，村民放弃耕作税负过重的土地、拒绝开罗权威的问题仍在继续。1865年，总督颁布敕令，禁止官员批准任何人放弃自己的土地。
同年晚些时候，他下令出售所有弃地的权利，以及任何未登记在税收登记册上的耕作土地的权利；同时，抛弃村庄者丧失权利的期限再次缩短，从五年减为三年。
同年另一道命令指出，尽管作出了和解努力，贝都因人仍拒绝服从总督的权威。指示称，任何阿拉伯人若在城镇、市场、道路或其他任何地方携带火器，都应予以逮捕。
同一时期还发布了数道命令，检查和整顿该国众多的监狱。
1865年6月，下尼罗河地区巡视官报告盗窃事件大幅增加，包括夜间袭击村庄和孤立的地产，抢走财物和牲畜。伊斯梅尔宣称这是邪恶歹徒所为，其中许多是前科犯，必须予以清除——办法是进一步监禁。他命令每个村庄和阿拉伯部落的首领在三十天内，把本地所有“堕落歹徒和可疑分子”缉拿归案。被捕者若体格合格，送陆军或海军；否则去尼罗河瀑布区的采石场做苦工。三十天后若在其辖区发现此类人物，头人本人将受惩罚。

en: Desertion of the land and armed rebellion were not the only problems the new agriculture faced. The extensive irrigation works required by industrial crops brought two additional forces into play: disease and debt. In May 1865, as the rebellion in the south subsided, cholera appeared. The cholera vibrio followed the same route an anticolonial militant from India would have taken, coming from South Asia to Mecca with the annual pilgrimage, then continuing on by boat across the Red Sea and overland to the Nile valley.
The main routes reached the Nile in the south, where the disease struck hardest. It claimed some sixty thousand lives, with the highest death rates in the provinces of Jirja and Asyut.

As with the gambiae malaria epidemic of the 1940s, the irrigation work in these two provinces exacerbated the disease. Villages that drew their water from the Nile escaped infection, while adjacent villages that used the standing water in the new canals suffered badly. In the town of Qina, near Jirja, 250 people were reported dead in a single day.“Shaikh Yussuf laid the mortality at Kenah to the canal water,” wrote a European resident, “which the poor people drink there.”

When the disease reached Alexandria in the north, it panicked the European business class and sent them fleeing. Thirty thousand left by ship within a fortnight, bringing all major commerce in the country to a standstill.
Their flight carried the cholera to all the main ports of the eastern and northern Mediterranean, helping turn the disease into a pandemic that circled the globe for a decade.
zh: 弃地和武装叛乱并非新农业面临的唯一问题。工业作物所需的大型灌溉工程，又引来了另外两股力量：疾病和债务。1865年5月，南方的叛乱平息之际，霍乱出现了。霍乱弧菌沿着一位印度反殖民斗士本来会走的路线传播：随一年一度的朝觐从南亚到麦加，再乘船渡过红海，经陆路进入尼罗河谷。
主要传播路线在南方抵达尼罗河，霍乱在那里最为肆虐。它夺走了约六万人的生命，吉尔贾省和艾斯尤特省的死亡率最高。
与20世纪40年代的冈比亚疟疾疫情一样，这两个省的灌溉工程加剧了疾病。从尼罗河取水的村庄未受感染，而使用新运河中积水的邻近村庄则受害严重。在吉尔贾附近的基纳镇，据报道一天之内就有250人死亡。“谢赫优素福把基纳的死亡归咎于运河里的水，”一位欧洲侨民写道，“穷人就在那里喝这种水。”
当疾病传到北方的亚历山大港时，欧洲商界陷入恐慌，纷纷逃离。两周内有三万人乘船离开，使该国所有主要商业陷于停顿。
他们的逃离把霍乱带到了地中海东部和北部的所有主要港口，使这场疾病演变为一场历时十年、环绕全球的大流行病。

en: Meanwhile, the cotton boom the country had enjoyed during the blockade of the Confederate ports in the American civil war had come to an end. Ismaʿil had taken large loans from European financiers during the boom years. One of the largest of these was in response to an earlier epidemic, the cattle murrain of the summer and autumn of 1863, which had killed anywhere from 250,000 to 900,000 head of cattle, wiping out most of the country’s draft animals used for ploughing and irrigation. Loans from European finance houses enabled Ismaʿil to import hundreds of thousands of animals from Europe and Asia, along with steam pumps and ploughs and emergency supplies of food.
But the food and the loans came too late to enable people to feed themselves that winter, and tens of thousands lost their lives.

The slump of 1865 was followed by the collapse of European speculative finance in the stock market crash of May 1866. Ismaʿil managed to obtain further loans to keep up interest payments to the banks. These loans only compounded the debt, however, postponing the crisis but making the eventual collapse more severe. The debt, as we shall see, was to provide a mechanism that would lever into place the new law of property, and with it the colonial occupation.
zh: 与此同时，美国内战期间南部邦联港口被封锁时该国享有的棉花繁荣已经结束。伊斯梅尔在繁荣年份从欧洲金融家那里借了大量贷款。其中最大的一笔贷款是为了应对此前一场疫情——1863年夏秋的牛瘟，它夺走了25万至90万头牛，使该国大部分用于耕作和灌溉的役畜死亡。来自欧洲金融机构的贷款使伊斯梅尔得以从欧洲和亚洲进口数十万头牲畜，以及蒸汽抽水机、犁和应急粮食。
但粮食和贷款来得太晚，人们无法在那个冬天养活自己，数万人丧生。
1865年的萧条之后，1866年5月的股市崩盘又使欧洲投机金融崩溃。伊斯梅尔设法获得更多贷款，以维持向银行支付利息。然而，这些贷款只是使债务更加沉重，推迟了危机，却使最终的崩溃更加严重。我们将看到，债务将提供一种机制，把新的产权法撬动到位，殖民占领也随之而来。

en: the private village
zh: 私人村庄

en: The obstacles to the consolidation of a new kind of control over the countryside included the occurrence of theft and armed attack, the continuing problem of desertion, the difficulty of establishing authority over the Arab population, the waves of modern epidemic disease, and what must have seemed the ever-present risk, demonstrated by the events in Jirja in 1865, of an armed revolt. These events, and the violence to which they were responding, constitute the local context that was omitted from the history of private property. Private property emerged in the form of large agricultural estates. Beginning by the 1840s, and expanding rapidly from the 1860s, the estates represented a further effort to find ways of establishing a detailed and continuous control over the rural population. This time it was more successful.
zh: 在乡村巩固一种新型控制所面临的障碍包括：盗窃和武装袭击的发生、持续不断的弃地问题、对阿拉伯人口建立权威的困难、一波波现代流行病，以及1865年吉尔贾事件所证明的、想必显得无时不在的武装起义风险。这些事件，以及它们所回应的暴力，构成了私有制史所省略的地方背景。私有产权以大型农业地产的形式出现。从19世纪40年代开始、自60年代起迅速扩张的地产，代表了为寻找对农村人口建立细致而持续控制的方法而作出的进一步努力。这一次较为成功。

en: By granting an estate to one of his functionaries, family members, or servants, the viceroy effectively subcontracted to the recipient, whether high-ranking officer or household coffee maker, the problem of policing and extracting revenue from that district. In fact the estate first emerged in the 1840s not as a form of private property, but as a means of making an individual official liable for paying the revenue arrears of a particular village. Any villager who owed taxes was thereby placed in debt bondage to the official and compelled to work the land to the benefit of the official until the debt had been paid.

(I will return in a moment to this issue of debt, a mechanism of coercion working within the right of property.) The estates Ismaʿil created in the 1860s and 1870s continued the practice of making villages or parts of villages the responsibility of individual officials. At the same time, the much lower tax rates on estates made them a potentially lucrative reward for the loyalty of those who received them. The reward provided a means of binding the recipient in allegiance to the ruler and thus strengthening his authority.
zh: 总督把一处地产赐给某个官员、家族成员或仆人，实际上就是把维持治安和从该地区抽取收入的问题转包给了受赐者——无论他是高级军官还是府中咖啡师。事实上，地产最初在19世纪40年代出现时并不是一种私有产权形式，而是一种让某个官员对特定村庄的欠税负责的手段。任何欠税的村民因此沦为该官员的债奴，被迫为官员的利益耕种土地，直到债务偿清。
（我稍后将回到债务问题，这是一种在产权权利内部运作的强制机制。）伊斯梅尔在19世纪60年代和70年代创设的地产，延续了让个别官员对村庄或部分村庄负责的做法。同时，地产上低得多的税率使它们成为对受赐者忠诚的潜在丰厚奖赏。这种奖赏提供了一种把受赐者束缚于对统治者效忠的手段，从而加强统治者的权威。

en: In the 1870s the estates were transformed from tax responsibilities into landholdings over which the recipient enjoyed what came to be called private ownership. This change did not occur because the holders sought the development of private rights. It was forced upon them by the government’s and the foreign bankers’ further demands for revenue. In 1871, sinking deeper into debt, the viceroy offered full ownership rights and the halving of future tax liability to anyone who would pay a sum equivalent to six years’ tax. The revenue from this arrangement was pledged to European bankers as security for another loan. The offer was unattractive to most landholders, so three years later the payment was made obligatory, in twelve annual installments. The “equivalent” (muqabala), as the payment was called, in effect a 50 percent increase in taxation, became the principal cause of indebtedness among landholders.

Private ownership emerged not as a right won by individuals against the state but as part of a penalty imposed upon them as a means of paying government debts, a penalty that in fact caused many smaller landholders to fall into debt themselves and lose their land.
zh: 19世纪70年代，地产从纳税责任转变为受赐者享有后来被称为私有产权的土地占有。这一变化并非因为持有人寻求发展私权而发生。它是政府和外国银行对收入的进一步要求强加给他们的。1871年，总督债台高筑，向任何愿意缴纳相当于六年税额款项的人提供完整所有权，并将未来税负减半。这项安排的收入被抵押给欧洲银行，作为另一笔贷款的担保。这项提议对大多数土地持有人没有吸引力，因此三年后改为强制缴纳，分十二期按年支付。这笔款项被称为“等值金”（muqabala），实际上相当于增税50%，成为土地持有人负债的主要原因。
私有产权并非作为个人向国家争取到的权利而出现，而是作为为偿还政府债务而施加于他们的一项惩罚的一部分；这项惩罚实际上使许多较小的土地持有人自己也陷入债务，失去了土地。

en: The advantage of the estate did not lie in higher productivity. The argument that large holdings were more productive than small farms was made after the British occupation and would be made again at the end of the twentieth century, as we will see, when the restrictions placed on the formation of estates in subsequent decades were once again removed. Small village farms were considered four times as productive as the large estates of the ruling family.

The estate’s advantage was that it enabled the most powerful households to achieve a direct and continuous control over the process of farming and claim complete possession of its product. The estate represented a system of supervision and coercion that succeeded for the first time in fixing cultivators permanently in place on the land and preventing them from abandoning cultivation or moving to another region. They could now be forced in large numbers to grow crops under the orders and for the benefit of an outsider.
zh: 地产的优势并不在于更高的生产力。大地产比小农场更具生产力的说法，是在英国占领之后提出的；我们将会看到，到20世纪末，当随后几十年间对地产形成的限制再次被取消时，这一说法又被重提。村里小农场的生产力被认为是统治家族大地产的四倍。
地产的优势在于，它使最有权势的家族得以对耕作过程实现直接而持续的控制，并主张对产品完全占有。地产代表了一套监督和强制体系，它首次成功地把耕种者永久固定在土地上，阻止他们放弃耕作或迁往其他地区。现在可以强迫大批人按照外来者的命令、为外来者的利益种植作物。

en: This power was achieved in several ways. First, the cultivators lost control not just of the land but of their households and living arrangements. They were made to live under close supervision in a “private village,” owned by the new owner of the land. Private landownership was in many cases the private ownership of a village.
zh: 这种权力通过几种方式实现。首先，耕种者失去控制的不仅是土地，还有他们的家庭和生活安排。他们被迫在严密监督下居住在一个“私人村庄”里，而这个村庄归土地的新主人所有。私有土地所有权在许多情况下就是对一座村庄的私人所有。

en: With the creation of large estates, especially those that brought former flood basins or wetlands under year-round cultivation, the owners required housing for the labor they used. At first they left the workers to construct their own huts, but they later discovered that greater power could be acquired over a workforce by taking control of their living arrangements. There were several recent precedents for the building of supervised accommodation for large groups of men, including the construction of barracks for a modern mass army and similar housing for the labor forces employed on major construction projects such as the Suez and Ibrahimiyya canals and the new railway lines.

There was even an attempt to control the accommodation of ordinary villagers, in the form of a program announced in 1846 to rebuild every village in the country according to a precise and regular plan. A number of model villages were built on the estates of the ruling family,“in order to show the fellahs how to construct their villages” (as the consultants Arthur D. Little were to try again a century later).

The sketch of the village of Gezzaye (see fig. 1), drawn by an Armenian engineer named Hekekyan, “shows the general style of these villages,” several of which were built in Lower and Upper Egypt. As the drawing indicates, the village consisted of three classes of houses: those for sheikhs and the well-to-do, those for “the middling class of fellahs,” and “lines of huts for the last class of fellahs.” A separate row of houses accommodated government officers and travelers, with a house of prostitution located conveniently behind. In the northwest corner, adjacent to the house of prostitution, was the manor house for the lord of the estate. The irregular size and shape of this compound, Hekekyan notes, represented a characteristic “derogation from the rule imposed on the rest of the place.” He added, however, that by the time of his visit about five years after the building of the village, “we found the streets already traversed in several directions by huts and stables in the manner of epaulements to secure privacy.”
zh: 随着大型地产的建立，尤其是那些把昔日的洪泛盆地或湿地改为全年耕作的庄园，业主需要为他们使用的劳动力提供住房。起初他们让工人自己搭建棚屋，但后来发现，控制工人的生活安排可以在劳动力身上获得更大的权力。为大批男性建造受监督的住所，此前已有几个先例，包括为现代大规模军队修建的营房，以及为苏伊士运河、易卜拉欣尼亚运河和新铁路等重大工程雇用的劳工修建的类似住房。
甚至还有控制普通村民住所的尝试，其形式是1846年宣布的一项计划：按照精确规则的规划重建全国每个村庄。统治家族的地产上建起了一些模范村，“以向费拉赫示范如何建造他们的村庄”（一个世纪后，阿瑟·D·利特尔咨询公司又尝试了一次）。

一位名叫赫基基扬的亚美尼亚工程师所绘的盖扎耶村草图（见图1），“显示了这些村庄的一般样式”，下埃及和上埃及都建有几个这样的村庄。如图所示，村庄有三类房屋：供谢赫和富裕人家居住的房屋、供“中等费拉赫阶层”居住的房屋，以及“供最下层费拉赫居住的一排排棚屋”。另有一排房屋供政府官员和旅行者居住，背后便利地设有一所妓院。西北角紧邻妓院的是庄园主的宅邸。赫基基扬指出，这个院落大小和形状不规则，代表着一种典型的“对施加于该地其余部分的规则的减损”。但他补充说，在村庄建成大约五年后他造访时，“我们发现街道已经被各个方向的棚屋和马厩横穿，像掩体一样用以保障私密。”

en: In the later part of the century, beginning once again on the viceregal estates, landowners began to construct large numbers of “organized” villages, in which “the owner imposed on his tenants a plan where everything had its logical place.” The typical layout consisted of several rows of mud huts to house the workers and their overseers, and at the center of these was the group of buildings known as the duwwar, consisting of a courtyard lined on three sides by storerooms and workshops and on the fourth by the offices, which had accommodation for the manager of the estate on an upper floor. On the largest estates the administration, housing the management offices and lodgings for the agricultural engineers, would be located at the center of the property or in the nearest village, while the workers would be housed in a series of compounds around the estate, each built as a walled enclosure with double doors set in a high gateway, like “a sort of fortress.” The housing formed a permanent “agricultural colony,” isolated from the main village and known as the ʿizba. By extension, the term
zh: 到该世纪后期，再次从总督的地产开始，地主们开始建造大量“有组织的”村庄，“业主把一套事事各得其所的规划强加给他的佃户”。典型的布局是几排土坯棚屋，供工人和监工居住；中央是一组称为“杜瓦尔”（duwwar）的建筑，由一座庭院构成，三面是储藏室和工场，第四面是办公室，其上层是地产管理人的住所。在最大的地产上，管理区——包括管理办公室和农业工程师的住所——位于地产中央或最近的村庄，而工人则住在环绕地产的一系列院落中，每个院落都是一座有围墙的围场，高大的门洞内设双扇门，像“某种堡垒”。这些住房形成一个永久的“农业殖民地”，与主村隔开，被称为“伊兹巴”（ʿizba）。由此引申，这个词
